title: Reuse canonical Fourfold PlaneSnapshot node-id tuples
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: PlaneSnapshot._sorted_node_ids always materialized a validation tuple, a duplicate-detection set, a sorted sequence, and a second tuple. The existing Forest-to-Fourfold adapter already supplies sorted immutable node-id tuples, so canonical Fourfold construction repeatedly paid this container/sort overhead even when no normalization was needed.
primary_claim: Fourfold plane node IDs are still validated exactly once and canonicalized deterministically, but an exact already-sorted unique tuple is now retained by object identity. Unsorted inputs are sorted after validation, and both adjacent and non-adjacent duplicates remain fail-closed. No Fourfold ontology, plane membership rule, Forest authority, relation semantics, or promotion authority changed.
gardener_decision: Remove redundant canonical-tuple rematerialization instead of adding a cache or parallel canonicalizer. Keep one bounded traversal for node validation/order detection, return an exact canonical tuple unchanged, and use the same local buffer for the sort fallback when input order actually requires repair.
